analysis: Docs-only change to docs/provider/cli-reference.md. The modified `darkbloom update` table (head lines 743-747) and the new paragraph (751-769) document `--rollback`, `--yes`, and rollback timeout/force semantics. I examined the visible text and the patch excerpt, which is truncated; it covers the documented rollback only. The text says rollback contacts no coordinator, restores the retained predecessor, and quarantines the installed release. It runs under the update lease via the watchdog's journaled rollback. It refuses if the kept release fails its hash or signature check, if the installed app is not the recorded release, if a cluster pair is serving, or if a provider runs outside launchd. These claims are consistent with T-043, where the watchdog rollback authority is the same replaceable binary, and with T-034 and T-013. The text introduces no new documented bypass. One residual point is that an operator-run rollback to a retained predecessor is a downgrade path. Coordinator-side release and qualification revocation (A-011, A-017, T-054) is platform-owned and outside the supplied evidence. The code (UpdateRollback.swift, SelfUpdater+Rollback.swift) is not supplied, so whether the rollback signature and hash check, the downgrade restriction, and the T-043 rollback-authority limits hold is unverified. The threat model may need T-043 or T-047 updated for the operator-initiated rollback command if that command is new in this PR; the visible text does not establish this. Other sections (logout, sandbox setup, addon hold, autopilot) appear to be unchanged context per file_changes ranges: head ranges 743-747, 751-769, 1852, and 1859-1860, and the last two are outside the supplied units. I found no concrete security regression in the documentation. Integration should check the code PRs for the rollback hash and signature verification, the lease, and the quarantine behavior.
